note: agent-lifted from VB's manuals (pilot steps 2 and 3)

concepts.label: WSS attenuation drift
concepts.gloss: A gradual deviation in a wavelength-selective switch's attenuation setting that leaves the affected optical channel underpowered after the node.
concepts.example: A WSS configured for 3 dB attenuation drifts to 7 dB, causing its routed channel to emerge at low power.

concepts.label: WSS passband shift
concepts.gloss: Misalignment of a WSS/ROADM spectral passband with an optical carrier, reducing that channel's quality even though its measured power can remain normal.
concepts.example: A 100 GHz ROADM filter shifts away from a 193.1 THz carrier, producing pre-FEC errors while channel power remains nominal.

concepts.label: WSS input port failure
concepts.gloss: Failure of one WSS input port that blocks all channels entering on its associated ROADM degree while channels from other degrees remain unaffected.
concepts.example: The west-degree WSS input fails, blocking every west-arriving wavelength but leaving east-degree traffic intact.

concepts.label: Transmit laser failure
synonyms: the far-end transmitter's laser has failed
concepts.gloss: Failure of the local or far-end transmitting laser that removes the launched optical signal and causes the corresponding remote receiver to lose that channel.
concepts.example: The laser on a VB-TPD-400 turns off, so the receiver at the opposite end reports loss of signal.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: A far-end equipment-card failure that removes carried traffic and monitoring, with traffic alarms potentially hidden by the equipment alarm.
concepts.example: A remote VB-OTN-LC-400 fails completely, making its channel and telemetry disappear while EQPT_CARD_FAIL masks secondary alarms.

concepts.label: Receiver degradation
synonyms: degradation of this unit's own receiver
concepts.gloss: Deterioration confined to a unit's own optical receiver that creates receive errors despite a normal optical path and normal reception on other channels.
concepts.example: A receiver front end becomes noisy and reports pre-FEC errors on one local channel although its incoming power and neighboring channels are normal.

concepts.label: a broken fibre
concepts.gloss: A physical break anywhere along an optical channel path that interrupts propagation of its light.
concepts.example: A cable cut between two sites prevents the channel from reaching the line receiver and leads to OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: a failed amplifier
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier on a channel path that has ceased providing usable optical output.
concepts.example: An inline EDFA loses its pump and goes dark, causing downstream receivers to lose all channels traversing it.

concepts.label: a disconnected patch cord
synonyms: the patch cord may have been disconnected
concepts.gloss: An unplugged optical patch lead on a channel path or at a multiplex-section input that breaks optical continuity.
concepts.example: A technician unplugs the patch cord feeding a preamplifier, causing OMS_LOS_P at the receiving end.

concepts.label: a blocked ROADM port
concepts.gloss: A ROADM port placed in, or failed into, a blocking state so that an intended channel cannot traverse its optical path.
concepts.example: The add port for 193.4 THz remains blocked after provisioning, and the far-end receiver raises OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: a rise in fibre loss
concepts.gloss: An increase in attenuation along a channel's fibre path that reduces received margin and can degrade or break OTU framing.
concepts.example: A bent span adds 5 dB of loss, raising pre-FEC errors until OTU_SD is reported.

concepts.label: a rise in an amplifier's noise
concepts.gloss: An increase in noise contributed by an amplifier on the channel path, lowering optical signal-to-noise ratio without necessarily removing light.
concepts.example: A deteriorating EDFA adds excess ASE noise, so OTU_SD appears while received power remains acceptable.

concepts.label: a rise in differential group delay
concepts.gloss: An increase in differential group delay along the optical path that introduces polarization-mode-dispersion impairment.
concepts.example: Changing fibre conditions raise DGD beyond the coherent receiver's tolerance and cause intermittent OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: a fast polarisation transient
concepts.gloss: A rapid change of optical polarization on the channel path that exceeds receiver tracking capability and causes transient errors or frame loss.
concepts.example: A fibre disturbance rotates polarization too quickly for the DSP, producing errored seconds and a brief OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: a dirty connector
concepts.gloss: Contamination on an optical connector that adds loss or reflections and degrades the traversing signal.
concepts.example: Dust on an LC connector raises pre-FEC BER above threshold and triggers OTU_SD.

concepts.label: any failure
concepts.gloss: An unspecified underlying fault used when an alarm indicates failure but the schema does not identify a more precise component or mechanism.
concepts.example: An OTU_BDI is correlated to an unknown remote failure when no specific failed resource can be determined.

concepts.label: Pump or unit failure
concepts.gloss: A complete optical-amplifier pump or unit failure that makes the amplifier output dark and loses every channel it carries.
concepts.example: The pump in a VB-OA-ILA stops, leaving no output light and dropping all downstream wavelengths.

concepts.label: Gain loss
concepts.gloss: Loss of gain within the current amplifier unit, resulting in low output power and reduced SNR across every carried channel.
concepts.example: A line amplifier delivers 5 dB less gain than configured, weakening all channels and reducing their OSNR.

concepts.label: Pump ageing
concepts.gloss: Progressive deterioration of an amplifier pump that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain and eventually reaches the pump end-of-life threshold.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-PRE pump current rises from 100% to 121% of its beginning-of-life value, triggering AMP_PUMP_EOL before traffic fails.

concepts.label: Gain tilt
concepts.gloss: A non-flat amplifier gain profile that weakens selected wavelengths, especially channels at one edge of the optical band, rather than all channels equally.
concepts.example: An EDFA provides 3 dB less gain at the long-wavelength band edge, so only those edge channels become weak.

concepts.label: the fibre section feeding this unit is broken
concepts.gloss: A break in the fibre section immediately upstream of the monitored unit that prevents input light from arriving.
concepts.example: The span feeding a VB-OA-ILA is cut, causing the amplifier to raise AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: its loss has risen sharply
concepts.gloss: A sharp increase in attenuation on the fibre section feeding a unit, potentially reducing its input below loss-of-signal thresholds.
concepts.example: A severe bend adds 15 dB on the incoming span, and the preamplifier raises OMS_LOS_P.

concepts.label: the preceding amplifier has failed and emits no light
concepts.gloss: Failure of the immediately upstream amplifier such that it emits no light toward the monitored unit.
concepts.example: The previous inline amplifier goes dark, causing the next line amplifier to report AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: failure of this unit's pump laser
concepts.gloss: Failure of the pump laser inside the current optical-amplifier unit, preventing normal amplification despite input light being present.
concepts.example: Input channels are visible at a VB-OA-BST, but its failed pump produces no output and AMP_FAIL is raised.

concepts.label: failure of the unit itself
concepts.gloss: A complete internal failure of the current amplifier unit, distinct from loss of its incoming optical signal.
concepts.example: A power-supply fault disables a VB-OA-PRE even though light reaches its input, resulting in AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: Switch fabric failure
concepts.gloss: Failure of an OTN switch's cross-connect fabric that interrupts ODUs traversing it and forwards alarm indication signals downstream.
concepts.example: The VB-OTNSW fabric fails, interrupting all cross-connected ODUs and causing AIS to be carried onward.

concepts.label: Wrong cross-connection
concepts.gloss: An erroneous ODU cross-connect in an OTN switch that delivers one ODU to the wrong destination without producing an optical-layer symptom.
concepts.example: After provisioning, ODU2 from client A is connected to client C instead of client B, causing ODU_TIM at C while optical power stays normal.

concepts.label: Client port failure
synonyms: a failure of the client port
concepts.gloss: Failure of a client-facing port or its optic at either service endpoint, causing the associated client service or received traffic to be lost.
concepts.example: A VB-CP-100GE optic fails at one endpoint, taking down the 100GE client service.

concepts.label: An impairment affecting the whole incoming line
concepts.gloss: An impairment common to the entire incoming WDM line whose effect is inherited by every channel routed onward through the node.
concepts.example: A noisy incoming amplified span lowers OSNR for all wavelengths, and each wavelength remains impaired after ROADM routing.

concepts.label: continues, after the node, as an impairment of each channel routed onwards
concepts.gloss: The persistence after a node of a line-wide impairment on each individual channel that the node forwards.
concepts.example: All channels entering with poor OSNR leave on different ROADM degrees with that poor OSNR still present.

concepts.label: A power loss upstream of up to about 8 dB
concepts.gloss: An upstream optical-power reduction of roughly 8 dB or less that a node can re-level, hiding low power downstream while retaining the associated SNR penalty.
concepts.example: A channel loses 6 dB before a ROADM, is restored to target output power there, but still has degraded OSNR.

concepts.label: is re-levelled at the node
concepts.gloss: A condition in which a node adjusts an incoming channel back to its configured output power level.
concepts.example: A channel arriving 4 dB low is equalized by the node to its nominal −2 dBm output.

concepts.label: does not appear downstream as low power
concepts.gloss: A condition in which upstream attenuation is no longer observable as low channel power after node equalization.
concepts.example: Downstream monitoring reads nominal power even though the channel was weak before the ROADM.

concepts.label: the loss of signal-to-noise ratio it caused remains
concepts.gloss: The residual signal-to-noise-ratio degradation that remains after optical power has been restored by a node.
concepts.example: After re-leveling restores a channel to −2 dBm, its OSNR remains 4 dB below baseline.

concepts.label: A larger loss
concepts.gloss: An upstream attenuation increase too large for node equalization to compensate, so reduced power continues downstream.
concepts.example: A 14 dB span loss exceeds the ROADM adjustment range and the channel exits the node underpowered.

concepts.label: passes on as low power
concepts.gloss: A condition in which a node forwards a channel while its optical power remains below target.
concepts.example: A channel arriving far below the equalizer range leaves the ROADM 8 dB low.

concepts.label: pass through the node unchanged
concepts.gloss: A condition or impairment that traverses a node without being corrected or otherwise altered.
concepts.example: A channel's DGD impairment is unchanged as it passes through an intermediate ROADM.

concepts.label: power is low
concepts.gloss: A per-channel condition in which optical power measured after a node is below its expected operating level.
concepts.example: The 193.1 THz channel measures −12 dBm after the ROADM instead of its −3 dBm target.

concepts.label: power is normal
concepts.gloss: A per-channel condition in which optical power remains within the expected range despite a possible non-power impairment.
concepts.example: A filtered channel reads its normal −3 dBm even while its pre-FEC BER rises.

concepts.label: signal quality is reduced
concepts.gloss: A per-channel degradation of signal integrity, such as reduced OSNR or increased errors, regardless of whether optical power is normal.
concepts.example: A shifted WSS passband increases pre-FEC BER on one channel while its power remains nominal.

concepts.label: is blocked
concepts.gloss: A condition in which every channel entering a node on one ROADM degree is prevented from passing at the failed point.
concepts.example: Failure of the west WSS input blocks all wavelengths arriving from the west degree.

concepts.label: are unaffected
concepts.gloss: A condition in which channels arriving on ROADM degrees other than the failed degree continue operating normally.
concepts.example: When the west input port fails, channels arriving from north and east remain in service.

concepts.label: no light reaches the receiver
synonyms: No light at the line receiver.
concepts.gloss: Absence of optical light at a line receiver, causing digital loss of signal and loss of OTU frame alignment.
concepts.example: Received power falls below detection, so the receiver declares G.798 dLOS and loses OTU framing.

concepts.label: declares loss of signal (G.798 dLOS)
concepts.gloss: The receiver's assertion of the G.798 digital loss-of-signal defect because no usable input signal is detected.
concepts.example: With the incoming fibre disconnected, the line receiver sets dLOS.

concepts.label: loses OTU frame alignment
concepts.gloss: Loss of synchronization to the framing structure of the received Optical Transport Unit signal.
concepts.example: After incoming light disappears, the receiver can no longer identify OTU frame boundaries.

concepts.label: the unit itself has failed
concepts.gloss: A condition in which the monitored equipment unit has internally failed, leading to an equipment defect, lost framing, and suppression of dependent traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A line card hardware failure declares dEQ, loses frame alignment, and masks its OTU traffic alarms.

concepts.label: declares an equipment defect (dEQ)
concepts.gloss: The unit's assertion of an equipment defect indicating an internal hardware or equipment-level failure.
concepts.example: A failed card processor causes the unit to declare dEQ.

concepts.label: frame alignment is lost
concepts.gloss: A receive condition in which OTU frame boundaries cannot be recovered, triggering downstream ODU-AIS insertion and a backward defect indication.
concepts.example: Severe signal impairment causes loss of frame alignment, after which the unit inserts ODU-AIS and sends BDI upstream.

concepts.label: the unit's traffic alarms are masked by the equipment alarm
concepts.gloss: Suppression of traffic-related alarms because a higher-level equipment alarm already identifies the failed unit.
concepts.example: When EQPT_CARD_FAIL is active, derived OTU_LOF alarms on that card are hidden.

concepts.label: the signal arrives but is impaired
concepts.gloss: A condition in which light and a signal reach the receiver but their quality is poor enough to cause pre-FEC errors or eventual frame loss.
concepts.example: A low-OSNR channel is present at the receiver but develops errors and later loses OTU alignment.

concepts.label: lower power, a lower signal-to-noise ratio, a raised differential group delay, a filtering penalty from a misaligned or narrowed passband, a receiver-side penalty, or a slow loss of margin
concepts.gloss: The class of optical or receiver impairments—including low power, low OSNR, excessive DGD, filter penalty, receiver penalty, or margin erosion—that can produce pre-FEC errors and frame loss.
concepts.example: A narrowed ROADM passband imposes a filtering penalty that first raises pre-FEC BER and then causes OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: pre-FEC errors appear
concepts.gloss: A condition in which bit errors are observed at the receiver before forward-error correction is applied.
concepts.example: The receiver records a pre-FEC BER of 2×10⁻³ while post-FEC traffic is still error-free.

concepts.label: Polarisation changes faster than the tracking range
concepts.gloss: An optical-polarization variation rate beyond the receiver's tracking range, causing transient decoding errors.
concepts.example: A rapid state-of-polarization rotation exceeds DSP tracking and creates several errored seconds.

concepts.label: produce errored seconds
concepts.gloss: A performance condition in which one or more seconds contain errors attributable to the current impairment.
concepts.example: A polarization transient causes five one-second intervals to be counted as errored seconds.

concepts.label: an ODU alarm indication signal is inserted downstream
concepts.gloss: Insertion of an ODU Alarm Indication Signal on downstream ODUs as the consequent action for an upstream framing defect.
concepts.example: After OTU frame loss, the line card sends ODU-AIS toward every downstream client mapped into that OTU.

concepts.label: a backward defect indication is sent
concepts.gloss: Transmission of a backward defect indication toward the far-end transmitter to report a receive-side defect.
concepts.example: A receiver that loses OTU framing returns BDI to the transmitting terminal.

concepts.label: loses the signal
concepts.gloss: Loss of a specific transmitted optical channel as observed by the receiver at the opposite end.
concepts.example: When the local transmit laser fails, the far-end receiver loses the 193.2 THz channel.

concepts.label: is lost
concepts.gloss: Complete absence of the referenced channel, traffic, carried channels, or client service at the relevant local, remote, or downstream observation point.
concepts.example: An amplifier output failure causes every channel it carries to be lost downstream.

concepts.label: goes silent
concepts.gloss: A condition in which monitoring or telemetry from a failed resource ceases entirely.
concepts.example: After the remote card crashes, its performance-monitoring counters stop updating.

concepts.label: are masked by the equipment alarm
concepts.gloss: A condition in which traffic alarms are suppressed or hidden because an equipment-level alarm is active.
concepts.example: OTU traffic alarms are masked while EQPT_CARD_FAIL identifies the failed card.

concepts.label: Errors appear
concepts.gloss: Errors observed only by the current receiver, indicating a local receive-side problem rather than a shared optical-path fault.
concepts.example: One receiver reports rising pre-FEC errors while another receiver on the same path remains normal.

concepts.label: are normal
concepts.gloss: A condition in which channels other than the affected one continue to meet normal operating criteria.
concepts.example: One locally degraded receiver reports errors, but all other channels remain error-free.

concepts.label: is normal
concepts.gloss: A condition in which the end-to-end optical path has normal power and quality, pointing away from a path impairment.
concepts.example: Path monitoring shows expected power and OSNR despite errors at one receiver.

concepts.label: OTU frame alignment lost while light is present.
concepts.gloss: Loss of OTU frame alignment while optical light is still present, distinguishing a quality or framing defect from optical loss of signal.
concepts.example: The receiver measures −4 dBm input power but cannot lock to OTU frames, so OTU_LOF is raised.

concepts.label: Signal degraded: pre-FEC errors above threshold
concepts.gloss: A signal-degrade condition declared when the pre-FEC error metric exceeds its configured threshold.
concepts.example: Pre-FEC BER rises above 1×10⁻³ for the hold-off period and triggers OTU_SD.

concepts.label: The far end reports a defect on the signal this unit transmits.
concepts.gloss: A backward indication from the remote endpoint that it detects a defect on the signal transmitted by the local unit.
concepts.example: The local line card receives BDI because the far-end receiver cannot frame the local OTU signal.

concepts.label: The unit has detected a fault in its transmit laser.
concepts.gloss: A locally detected hardware fault in the unit's transmit laser or its drive circuitry.
concepts.example: Laser bias telemetry goes out of range and the unit raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

concepts.label: Card hardware fault.
concepts.gloss: An equipment condition indicating that a card has suffered an internal hardware failure.
concepts.example: A failed card power rail causes EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

concepts.label: All three units operate
concepts.gloss: The normal amplifier-chain condition in which booster, line, and preamplifier units are all operational and regulate their configured gain.
concepts.example: The BA, ILA, and PA each remain active and hold their target gain across the multiplex section.

concepts.label: constant-gain mode
concepts.gloss: An amplifier operating mode that regulates output so the configured optical gain remains constant as input power varies.
concepts.example: When span input drops by 2 dB, the EDFA increases output effort to preserve 20 dB gain.

concepts.label: less light arrives at the input
concepts.gloss: A reduction in total optical power arriving at an amplifier input that leads to reduced output light and lower per-channel OSNR.
concepts.example: A span adds 3 dB loss, so the line amplifier receives less light and its output channels have poorer OSNR.

concepts.label: less light leaves the output
concepts.gloss: A reduction in optical power emitted from an amplifier output as a consequence of reduced input or insufficient gain.
concepts.example: After input power falls 5 dB, the amplifier output is also below its normal total power.

concepts.label: the optical signal-to-noise ratio of every channel falls as well
concepts.gloss: A reduction in optical signal-to-noise ratio across every channel affected by the amplifier or line condition.
concepts.example: All 80 wavelengths lose about 2 dB of OSNR after a weak amplifier input.

concepts.label: Loss of the OSC on one section
concepts.gloss: Loss of the optical supervisory channel on a single fibre section, confined to that section rather than automatically cascading across subsequent sections.
concepts.example: The OSC receiver at one ILA loses its upstream supervisory carrier, while the next section generates and receives its own OSC normally.

concepts.label: does not propagate to the next
concepts.gloss: A condition in which a section-local defect is terminated and is not reproduced on the following network section.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS on span A–B is visible at B but does not cause OSC_LOS on span B–C.

concepts.label: no light arrives
concepts.gloss: Complete absence of optical input to a unit, causing that unit to emit no carried light.
concepts.example: A fibre cut removes all input to an inline amplifier, so no WDM channels leave its output.

concepts.label: no light leaves
concepts.gloss: Complete absence of emitted optical light at a unit's output.
concepts.example: The output power monitor reads below detection and downstream receivers lose all wavelengths.

concepts.label: the input is weak
concepts.gloss: An amplifier input condition in which incoming optical power is below its normal range, producing a weak and noisier output.
concepts.example: A line amplifier receives −30 dBm total power and emits channels with low power and degraded OSNR.

concepts.label: the output is weak
concepts.gloss: An output condition in which emitted optical power is below the required operating level.
concepts.example: The amplifier output is 6 dB below its configured total-power target.

concepts.label: the output is noisier
concepts.gloss: An output condition in which the signal contains more amplifier noise and therefore lower OSNR than normal.
concepts.example: The amplifier restores some power but adds enough ASE that each channel loses 3 dB of OSNR.

concepts.label: the output goes dark
concepts.gloss: Complete loss of optical output from the amplifier unit, affecting the unit's entire output rather than an individual channel.
concepts.example: A pump failure drives the VB-OA-ILA output below detection for all wavelengths.

concepts.label: Output power is low
concepts.gloss: An amplifier condition in which output power is below target for every channel it carries.
concepts.example: Gain loss leaves all 40 channels 4 dB below their expected output levels.

concepts.label: the signal-to-noise ratio falls
concepts.gloss: A reduction in signal-to-noise ratio affecting every channel traversing the impaired unit.
concepts.example: Excess amplifier noise lowers OSNR on every wavelength by 2 dB.

concepts.label: raises its drive current to hold the gain
concepts.gloss: The amplifier's compensating action of increasing pump-laser drive current to preserve configured gain as the pump ages.
concepts.example: The controller raises pump current from 100% to 112% of beginning-of-life current to maintain 20 dB gain.

concepts.label: Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit
concepts.gloss: Continued normal traffic delivery while pump-current compensation remains below its operating limit.
concepts.example: At 115% pump current the amplifier still holds gain, so no client packets are lost.

concepts.label: gives early warning
concepts.gloss: A maintenance indication derived from a deteriorating trend before that deterioration causes service impact.
concepts.example: A steadily rising pump-current graph warns operations weeks before an end-of-life alarm.

concepts.label: leads eventually to the end-of-life alarm (AMP_PUMP_EOL)
concepts.gloss: The progression of an ageing-pump trend to the AMP_PUMP_EOL alarm once the configured current threshold is reached.
concepts.example: Pump current rises past 120% of beginning-of-life value and AMP_PUMP_EOL is asserted.

concepts.label: arrive weaker than the others
concepts.gloss: A relative-power condition in which channels at one edge of the optical band reach the receiver below the level of central channels.
concepts.example: C-band edge channels arrive 3 dB weaker than mid-band channels because of gain tilt.

concepts.label: are affected
concepts.gloss: A selective impairment condition that applies to some channels but not to the full carried spectrum.
concepts.example: Only the four longest-wavelength channels show low power; the remaining channels are normal.

concepts.label: no light arrives at its input
concepts.gloss: Absence of all optical light at a line amplifier's input, used as the trigger condition for AMP_INPUT_LOS.
concepts.example: A span cut makes the VB-OA-ILA input monitor read no light and raises AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: no light arrives at the input of the receiving end of the multiplex section
concepts.gloss: Absence of optical light at the receiving end input of an optical multiplex section, used to declare OMS loss of signal.
concepts.example: No WDM power reaches the preamplifier at the far end, so OMS_LOS_P is raised.

concepts.label: the supervisory channel is not received
concepts.gloss: Failure to receive the optical supervisory channel at a line-amplifier or preamplifier input.
concepts.example: The payload wavelengths remain detectable but the OSC carrier is absent, causing OSC_LOS.

concepts.label: light is present at its input but none leaves its output
concepts.gloss: An amplifier failure signature in which optical input is present but no optical signal emerges from the output.
concepts.example: The input monitor reads −5 dBm while the output is dark, so AMP_FAIL is raised.

concepts.label: the gain departs from its set point by more than 2 dB
concepts.gloss: An amplifier condition in which actual gain differs from its configured set point by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: A 20 dB gain target measures 17.5 dB, triggering AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: the pump drive current exceeds 120 per cent of its beginning-of-life value
concepts.gloss: An amplifier pump-age threshold condition in which drive current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: Pump telemetry reaches 122%, causing AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: an ODU alarm indication signal
concepts.gloss: An ODU Alarm Indication Signal representing an upstream ODU defect and causing downstream AIS propagation and client-service loss.
concepts.example: A failed upstream OTU inserts ODU-AIS, which the OTN switch forwards and the client port treats as service down.

concepts.label: carries an ODU alarm indication signal onwards on every ODU cross-connected through it
concepts.gloss: Forwarding of ODU-AIS by an OTN switch on every ODU cross-connection affected by the incoming indication.
concepts.example: The switch receives AIS on a failed aggregate ODU and carries it onward on each mapped downstream ODU.

concepts.label: an ODU delivered from the wrong source
concepts.gloss: An ODU delivered from a source other than the one provisioned or expected at the destination.
concepts.example: Client B receives client A's ODU after an incorrect cross-connect, taking B's intended service down.

concepts.label: takes the client service down
concepts.gloss: A condition in which the client-facing service is unavailable because the delivered ODU is defective, alarmed, or from the wrong source.
concepts.example: Reception of ODU-AIS causes the 100GE client service to go down.

concepts.label: the service is protected
concepts.gloss: A service configuration with an alternate path that can be selected after a defect on the active path.
concepts.example: A 100GE service has working and protection ODU paths through separate switches.

concepts.label: the selector can choose a path free of defects
concepts.gloss: Availability to the protection selector of at least one candidate path without relevant defects.
concepts.example: When the working ODU fails, the selector finds the protection ODU healthy and switches to it.

concepts.label: the service suffers only a brief hit while the selector switches
concepts.gloss: A short service interruption limited to the interval required for a protection selector to change paths.
concepts.example: Traffic pauses for 30 ms while the selector moves from the failed working path to protection.

concepts.label: is interrupted
concepts.gloss: Loss of continuity for every ODU cross-connected through a failed OTN switch fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric outage stops all ODUs traversing the VB-OTNSW.

concepts.label: an alarm indication signal is carried onwards
concepts.gloss: Propagation of an alarm indication signal on each affected ODU beyond the point of interruption.
concepts.example: After fabric failure, each downstream ODU carries AIS toward its client port.

concepts.label: is delivered to the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: Delivery of one ODU to a destination other than its provisioned endpoint because of an incorrect cross-connect.
concepts.example: ODU A appears on client port C instead of client port B.

concepts.label: There is no optical symptom.
concepts.gloss: Absence of any optical-power or light-loss indication for an ODU-layer routing defect.
concepts.example: Power and OTU framing remain normal even though the switch sends the ODU to the wrong client.

concepts.label: fails
concepts.gloss: A failure state affecting a client optic and its associated client port.
concepts.example: The 100GE pluggable stops transmitting, placing the port in a failed state.

concepts.label: The client service has failed.
concepts.gloss: A condition indicating that the service presented on a client port is no longer operational.
concepts.example: Loss of the client optic causes the port to declare CLIENT_SF.

concepts.label: An ODU alarm indication signal is received.
concepts.gloss: Reception at a client port of an ODU Alarm Indication Signal from upstream.
concepts.example: The egress client port detects the ODU-AIS pattern and raises ODU_AIS.

concepts.label: The far end reports that it is receiving an alarm indication signal.
concepts.gloss: A backward report that the remote endpoint is receiving an alarm indication signal on the ODU.
concepts.example: The local client port raises ODU_BDI after the far end reports incoming AIS.

concepts.label: Trail trace identifier mismatch: the ODU received is not the one expected.
concepts.gloss: Mismatch between the received ODU trail trace identifier and the identifier provisioned for the expected ODU.
concepts.example: Port C expects trace ID CLIENT-C but receives CLIENT-A and raises ODU_TIM.

concepts.label: The selector is on the protection path.
concepts.gloss: A protection-state condition in which the service selector currently forwards traffic over the protection ODU path.
concepts.example: Following a working-path defect, the selector switches to protection and PROT_ACTIVE is shown.

concepts.label: The protection path has failed.
concepts.gloss: A condition in which the standby or selected protection path is defective and unavailable for reliable protection.
concepts.example: The backup ODU loses framing, causing PROT_UNAVAIL.

concepts.label: Port hardware fault.
concepts.gloss: An internal hardware defect in a client port, distinct from a remote service or ODU-path defect.
concepts.example: A failed port PHY causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL on a VB-CP-100GE.

concepts.label: Fabric fault.
concepts.gloss: An internal hardware or functional defect of an OTN switch fabric.
concepts.example: The cross-connect ASIC fails self-test and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

concepts.label: the power of every channel
concepts.gloss: The measured optical power of each individual wavelength channel, available when a node has the channel-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A channel monitor reports −3.1 dBm for 193.1 THz and −4.0 dBm for 193.2 THz.

concepts.label: the OSNR of every channel
concepts.gloss: The measured optical signal-to-noise ratio of each individual wavelength channel, available with channel monitoring.
concepts.example: The node reports 21 dB OSNR for one channel and 17 dB for another.

concepts.label: Received power
concepts.gloss: The optical power measured at a unit's receiver, supported across the listed transponder, muxponder, and OTN line-card units when power monitoring is available.
concepts.example: A VB-TPD-400 reports received power of −6.2 dBm.

concepts.label: errored seconds, in 15-minute bins
concepts.gloss: The count of one-second intervals containing errors, accumulated and reported in 15-minute performance bins by all listed terminal units.
concepts.example: A VB-MXP-400 reports 12 errored seconds for the 10:00–10:15 interval.

concepts.label: Optical power
concepts.gloss: A monitored optical-power value exposed by units equipped with the power-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A unit reports −5.5 dBm at its monitored optical interface.

concepts.label: Estimated OSNR
concepts.gloss: A receiver- or DSP-derived estimate of optical signal-to-noise ratio available with advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: Advanced telemetry estimates the received channel OSNR at 18.7 dB.

concepts.label: pre-FEC bit error ratio
concepts.gloss: The ratio of erroneous received bits before forward-error correction, available through advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: The line card reports a pre-FEC BER of 8×10⁻⁴.

concepts.label: differential group delay
concepts.gloss: The measured delay difference between principal polarization modes of the received optical signal, exposed by advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: The coherent receiver reports 18 ps of DGD.

concepts.label: polarisation change rate
concepts.gloss: The measured rate at which the received signal's state of polarization changes, available with advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: Telemetry shows a polarization rotation rate above the receiver's tracking threshold.

concepts.label: Total optical power at the unit's input
concepts.gloss: The aggregate optical power of all light measured at a unit's input when power monitoring is installed.
concepts.example: An amplifier reports total input power of −8 dBm across 40 channels.

concepts.label: Total optical power at the unit's output
concepts.gloss: The aggregate optical power of all light measured at a unit's output when power monitoring is installed.
concepts.example: A booster reports +17 dBm total output power.

concepts.label: Drive current of the pump laser, as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value
concepts.gloss: The amplifier pump-laser drive current normalized as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value and available through advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: A five-year-old amplifier reports pump drive current at 116%.

concepts.label: an indicator of pump health
concepts.gloss: An advanced-monitoring indicator summarizing the condition or remaining margin of an amplifier pump.
concepts.example: The management system marks pump health as degraded after a sustained current increase.

concepts.label: Presence of the supervisory channel at the input
concepts.gloss: A status measurement indicating whether the optical supervisory channel is present at a unit's input.
concepts.example: An ILA reports OSC presence=false after an upstream span fault.

concepts.label: client errored seconds
concepts.gloss: The number of one-second client-interface intervals containing errors, reported by each client port in 15-minute bins.
concepts.example: A 100GE client port reports three client errored seconds from 12:00 to 12:15.

concepts.label: client unavailable seconds
concepts.gloss: The number of seconds for which a client interface was unavailable, reported by each client port in 15-minute bins.
concepts.example: A failed optic produces 900 client unavailable seconds in one 15-minute interval.

concepts.label: ROADM
concepts.gloss: A reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer using WSS functions to route wavelength channels and subject to attenuation drift, passband shift, and input-port failure.
concepts.example: The VB-ROADM-CDC routes a 193.1 THz channel from the west degree to the east degree.

concepts.label: colourless, directionless and contentionless ROADM
concepts.gloss: A ROADM that can add or drop any wavelength on any direction without fixed wavelength ports or contention restrictions.
concepts.example: A colourless, directionless, contentionless node assigns two same-frequency services to different add/drop resources and line degrees.

concepts.label: Transponder
concepts.gloss: A terminal optical resource that converts a client signal to and from a single line-side wavelength channel.
concepts.example: A VB-TPD-400 maps a 400GE client signal onto one coherent optical channel.

concepts.label: Muxponder
concepts.gloss: A terminal resource that multiplexes multiple lower-rate client signals into a higher-rate optical line signal and demultiplexes them on receive.
concepts.example: A VB-MXP-400 combines four 100GE clients into one 400G line channel.

concepts.label: OTN line card
concepts.gloss: A card that terminates OTN line signals and provides OTU/ODU framing, monitoring, and transport functions.
concepts.example: A VB-OTN-LC-400 terminates an OTU4-like line signal and exposes its ODUs to the switch.

concepts.label: All units
concepts.gloss: The collective class of VB transponders, muxponders, and OTN line cards that share receiver, transmitter, card-fault, and performance-monitoring behavior.
concepts.example: A VB-TPD-400 and VB-OTN-LC-400 can both raise OTU_LOF and report 15-minute errored seconds.

concepts.label: Booster amplifier (BA)
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier placed after a transmitting ROADM to raise multiplex-section launch power and subject to pump, gain, ageing, and tilt faults.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-BST boosts the ROADM output before it enters the outgoing fibre span.

concepts.label: At the transmitting end of a multiplex section, after the ROADM
concepts.gloss: The network placement immediately after the transmitting-end ROADM and before the outgoing multiplex-section fibre.
concepts.example: At site A, the booster sits between the ROADM degree output and the A–B line fibre.

concepts.label: Line amplifier (LA)
concepts.gloss: An intermediate-site optical amplifier that restores WDM line power along a multiplex section and monitors its incoming span.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-ILA amplifies the WDM signal midway between terminal sites.

concepts.label: At intermediate amplifier sites
concepts.gloss: The placement of a line amplifier at an intermediate site between the transmitting and receiving ends of a multiplex section.
concepts.example: An ILA is installed at the midpoint hut on a 160 km optical route.

concepts.label: Preamplifier (PA)
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier at the receiving end of a multiplex section, before the ROADM, that raises incoming line power for node reception.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-PRE amplifies the incoming WDM line immediately before the receive-side ROADM.

concepts.label: At the receiving end of a multiplex section, before the ROADM
concepts.gloss: The network placement at the receiving end of a multiplex section between the incoming fibre and the ROADM.
concepts.example: At site B, the preamplifier is connected after the A–B span and before B's ROADM.

concepts.label: OTN switch
concepts.gloss: An equipment resource that cross-connects ODUs through a switching fabric and can suffer fabric failures or erroneous cross-connections.
concepts.example: The VB-OTNSW maps an incoming ODU2 from a line card to a 100GE client port.

concepts.label: ODU cross-connect fabric
concepts.gloss: The internal OTN switching fabric that establishes cross-connections between incoming and outgoing ODU tributaries.
concepts.example: The ODU fabric connects ODU2 port 1/1 to egress port 4/3.

concepts.label: Client port, 10GE
concepts.gloss: A 10 Gigabit Ethernet client-facing port resource that can experience client-port hardware or optic failure.
concepts.example: A VB-CP-10GE accepts a customer's 10GE signal for OTN transport.

concepts.label: Client port, 100GE
concepts.gloss: A 100 Gigabit Ethernet client-facing port resource that can experience client-port hardware or optic failure.
concepts.example: A VB-CP-100GE maps a customer 100GE service into an ODU.

concepts.label: Client port, 400GE
concepts.gloss: A 400 Gigabit Ethernet client-facing port resource that can experience client-port hardware or optic failure.
concepts.example: A VB-CP-400GE terminates a 400GE client and feeds the OTN line system.

concepts.label: client port
concepts.gloss: The generic class of 10GE, 100GE, and 400GE client-facing ports on which service, ODU, protection, and equipment alarms are reported.
concepts.example: A VB-CP-100GE raises CLIENT_SF after its client optic fails.

concepts.label: OCH_LOS
concepts.gloss: An optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm raised by a terminal unit when no light reaches its line receiver, commonly due to transmitter, card, path, amplifier, patching, or ROADM blockage faults.
concepts.example: A cut fibre removes channel light at a VB-TPD-400 receiver, which raises OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: OTU_LOF
concepts.gloss: An OTU loss-of-frame alarm raised when light is present but OTU frame alignment is lost because of severe optical or receiver impairment.
concepts.example: Excess DGD prevents a VB-MXP-400 from framing the OTU signal, so it raises OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: OTU_SD
concepts.gloss: An OTU signal-degrade alarm raised when pre-FEC errors exceed threshold, indicating reduced margin before total frame loss.
concepts.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER above the configured limit and a VB-OTN-LC-400 raises OTU_SD.

concepts.label: OTU_BDI
concepts.gloss: An OTU backward-defect-indication alarm showing that the far end reports a defect on the signal transmitted by this unit.
concepts.example: A local transponder raises OTU_BDI after the remote receiver loses frame alignment.

concepts.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An equipment alarm raised by a terminal unit when it detects failure of its own transmit laser.
concepts.example: A VB-TPD-400 detects missing laser output and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

concepts.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An equipment alarm raised when a transponder, muxponder, or OTN line card detects an internal card hardware fault.
concepts.example: A failed FPGA on a VB-MXP-400 causes EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

concepts.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
concepts.gloss: A line-amplifier alarm indicating that no light reaches its input because of an upstream fibre, loss, or preceding-amplifier problem.
concepts.example: A broken feeding span causes a VB-OA-ILA to raise AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: OMS_LOS_P
concepts.gloss: A preamplifier alarm indicating loss of all optical multiplex-section light at the receiving-end input.
concepts.example: A disconnected receive-side patch cord causes the VB-OA-PRE to raise OMS_LOS_P.

concepts.label: OSC_LOS
concepts.gloss: An alarm raised by a line amplifier or preamplifier when the optical supervisory channel is not received from the feeding section.
concepts.example: A severe upstream loss removes the OSC at an ILA, which raises OSC_LOS.

concepts.label: AMP_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An optical-amplifier failure alarm raised when input light is present but no output light is produced, usually because of pump or unit failure.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-BST has normal input power but a dark output after pump failure, so it raises AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
concepts.gloss: An alarm raised by a line amplifier or preamplifier when measured gain differs from its set point by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: A preamplifier set to 20 dB delivers 17 dB and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
concepts.gloss: An amplifier pump end-of-life alarm raised when pump drive current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-ILA reports 123% pump current and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: CLIENT_SF
concepts.gloss: A client-port service-failure alarm indicating that the client service is down because of a port, ODU routing, switch-fabric, or other failure.
concepts.example: A wrong ODU cross-connect deprives a VB-CP-100GE of its expected service and CLIENT_SF is raised.

concepts.label: ODU_AIS
concepts.gloss: A client-port alarm indicating that an ODU Alarm Indication Signal has been received from upstream.
concepts.example: An upstream OTU failure inserts AIS, and the egress client port raises ODU_AIS.

concepts.label: ODU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A client-port ODU backward-defect alarm indicating that the far end reports receiving an alarm indication signal.
concepts.example: The remote client receives ODU-AIS and reports it backward, causing the local port to raise ODU_BDI.

concepts.label: ODU_TIM
concepts.gloss: An ODU trail-trace-identifier-mismatch alarm raised when a client port receives an ODU other than the one provisioned.
concepts.example: A wrong cross-connect delivers trace ID A to a port expecting B, which raises ODU_TIM.

concepts.label: PROT_ACTIVE
concepts.gloss: A protection-status alarm or indication showing that a client service selector is currently using the protection path.
concepts.example: After the working ODU fails, the selector moves to backup and the port reports PROT_ACTIVE.

concepts.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
concepts.gloss: A protection alarm indicating that the configured protection path has failed and cannot provide backup service.
concepts.example: Loss of framing on the standby ODU causes the client port to raise PROT_UNAVAIL.

concepts.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A client-port equipment alarm indicating an internal port hardware fault.
concepts.example: A failed Ethernet PHY on a VB-CP-400GE raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

concepts.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An OTN-switch equipment alarm indicating a fault in the ODU cross-connect fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric ASIC failure in VB-OTNSW raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

concepts.label: The channel
concepts.gloss: The single optical wavelength channel to which a stated condition or fault consequence applies.
concepts.example: For a passband shift at 193.1 THz, the channel scope is only that 193.1 THz service.

concepts.label: Every channel arriving at the node on that degree
concepts.gloss: All wavelength channels entering a ROADM node through one specified line degree.
concepts.example: The scope includes every wavelength arriving on the west degree when its WSS input fails.

concepts.label: channels arriving on the other degrees
concepts.gloss: Channels entering the same ROADM through degrees other than the degree associated with the fault.
concepts.example: If the west input fails, channels on the north and east degrees are the other-degree channels.

concepts.label: The channel it transmits
concepts.gloss: The particular optical channel launched by the unit's transmitter and potentially observed as lost at the far end.
concepts.example: The transmitted channel is the 193.2 THz carrier emitted by a VB-TPD-400.

concepts.label: the traffic it receives
concepts.gloss: The payload traffic arriving at and accepted by a unit or port from its peer.
concepts.example: A remote card failure removes the 100GE traffic received at the local endpoint.

concepts.label: its monitoring
concepts.gloss: The telemetry and performance-monitoring output associated with a particular resource.
concepts.example: After a card goes silent, its power and error counters constitute the missing monitoring scope.

concepts.label: its traffic alarms
concepts.gloss: The set of service- and signal-related alarms generated by a particular unit for its carried traffic.
concepts.example: OTU_LOF and OTU_SD on a failed line card are within its traffic-alarm scope.

concepts.label: this receiver only
concepts.gloss: A scope restricted to the current receiver, excluding the shared path and other receivers or channels.
concepts.example: Errors seen only by receiver 1, while receiver 2 remains normal, have receiver-only scope.

concepts.label: other channels
concepts.gloss: All channels relevant to the comparison except the specifically affected channel.
concepts.example: When one channel's receiver degrades, the remaining 39 wavelengths are the other channels.

concepts.label: the optical path
concepts.gloss: The end-to-end physical and optical route traversed by a channel between transmitter and receiver.
concepts.example: The optical path includes patching, ROADMs, fibre spans, and amplifiers from site A to site B.

concepts.label: the unit
concepts.gloss: The complete monitored equipment unit to which a condition applies, rather than one individual channel.
concepts.example: A dark amplifier output affects the whole VB-OA-ILA unit.

concepts.label: Every channel carried by the unit
concepts.gloss: All wavelength channels transported through a given optical unit.
concepts.example: The 80 wavelengths passing through a line amplifier are its channels carried.

concepts.label: every channel
concepts.gloss: The entire set of channels under the referenced resource or event, with no channel excluded.
concepts.example: Gain loss lowers output power on every channel through the amplifier.

concepts.label: Traffic
concepts.gloss: The payload service traffic whose continuity or quality is being described.
concepts.example: During early pump ageing, the traffic scope remains unaffected.

concepts.label: the trend
concepts.gloss: The time-series behavior of a monitored metric used to detect progressive deterioration.
concepts.example: The month-by-month rise in pump current is the trend used for early warning.

concepts.label: channels at one edge of the band
concepts.gloss: Wavelength channels located near one boundary of the amplifier's supported optical band.
concepts.example: The longest-wavelength four channels at the edge of the C-band are weakened by gain tilt.

concepts.label: Some channels, not all
concepts.gloss: A proper subset of carried channels, explicitly not the whole set.
concepts.example: Five of 80 wavelengths show low power while the other 75 remain normal.

concepts.label: Every ODU cross-connected through the switch
concepts.gloss: All ODU connections whose configured routes traverse the specified OTN switch fabric.
concepts.example: Twenty ODU2 services cross-connected through VB-OTNSW are all interrupted by its fabric failure.

concepts.label: each
concepts.gloss: Each individual ODU among the set affected by an OTN switching or AIS-propagation event.
concepts.example: AIS is placed on each ODU that crossed the failed fabric.

concepts.label: one ODU
concepts.gloss: A single ODU connection, as opposed to all ODUs carried by a switch or line signal.
concepts.example: A wrong cross-connect misroutes one ODU while unrelated ODUs remain correct.

concepts.label: The client optic
concepts.gloss: The optical transceiver or pluggable that implements the client-facing physical interface.
concepts.example: The QSFP-DD in a VB-CP-400GE is the client optic.

concepts.label: the port
concepts.gloss: The complete client-port resource, including its interface electronics and operational state.
concepts.example: A PHY hardware failure affects the whole 100GE port.

concepts.label: the client service
concepts.gloss: The customer-facing service carried through a client port and its associated ODU path.
concepts.example: The 100GE connection between customer routers is the client service lost after ODU-AIS.

concepts.label: after the node
concepts.gloss: The observation point on the outgoing side of a network node after its switching or equalization functions.
concepts.example: Channel power measured at the ROADM degree output is measured after the node.

concepts.label: there
concepts.gloss: The same local point associated with the referenced fault or resource, used as the observation location of its effect.
concepts.example: Channels are blocked there—at the failed WSS input within the node.

concepts.label: The receiver at the far end
concepts.gloss: The receiver at the remote endpoint corresponding to the current unit's transmitter.
concepts.example: For a transmitter at site A, the far-end receiver is the line receiver at site B.

concepts.label: the far end
concepts.gloss: The remote endpoint of the monitored bidirectional service or trail.
concepts.example: A local card at site A treats the peer card at site B as the far end.

concepts.label: here
concepts.gloss: The local monitored endpoint or node from whose perspective the condition is described.
concepts.example: A downstream AIS arriving at the current client port is observed here.

concepts.label: this receiver
concepts.gloss: The specific local receiver currently under diagnosis or reporting the condition.
concepts.example: Errors appear at this receiver on port 1/1 but not at the peer receiver.

concepts.label: the far-end transmitter
concepts.gloss: The remote transmitter that sends the optical signal received by the current local receiver.
concepts.example: For a receiver at site B, the associated laser at site A is the far-end transmitter.

concepts.label: along the channel's path
concepts.gloss: Any point along the end-to-end optical route followed by a particular wavelength channel.
concepts.example: A broken fibre midway between ROADMs lies along the channel path.

concepts.label: the line receiver
concepts.gloss: The optical receiver that terminates the network-facing OTU line signal.
concepts.example: The coherent line receiver on a VB-OTN-LC-400 detects incoming channel light.

concepts.label: this unit's own receiver
concepts.gloss: The receive function physically contained in the current equipment unit.
concepts.example: A noisy coherent front end on the local muxponder is its own receiver.

concepts.label: on the path to the far end
concepts.gloss: The transport route from the current endpoint toward its remote peer.
concepts.example: A failed inline amplifier on the A-to-B route lies on the path to the far end.

concepts.label: the signal this unit transmits
concepts.gloss: The optical or OTN signal emitted by the current unit and evaluated by the far-end receiver.
concepts.example: The local 400G OTU carrier is the transmitted signal on which the far end reports a defect.

concepts.label: on this unit
concepts.gloss: A location on or within the currently referenced equipment unit rather than on the remote peer or intervening path.
concepts.example: A locally detected transmit-laser failure is on this unit.

concepts.label: this unit
concepts.gloss: The current managed equipment instance whose alarms, measurements, or internal faults are being discussed.
concepts.example: For AMP_GAIN_OOR on ILA-7, this unit is ILA-7.

concepts.label: this card
concepts.gloss: The particular equipment card currently being monitored or diagnosed.
concepts.example: A failed FPGA is located on this card, VB-OTN-LC-400 slot 3.

concepts.label: the output
concepts.gloss: The egress optical interface of the referenced unit where emitted power is observed.
concepts.example: A power meter at the amplifier output detects no light.

concepts.label: downstream
concepts.gloss: The direction or set of resources reached after the current point in the signal's forwarding direction.
concepts.example: ODU-AIS inserted by the receiver is observed at downstream client ports.

concepts.label: the fibre section feeding this unit
concepts.gloss: The immediately upstream fibre span that delivers optical light into the current unit.
concepts.example: For ILA-2, the fibre from ILA-1 to ILA-2 is its feeding fibre section.

concepts.label: the preceding amplifier
concepts.gloss: The nearest upstream amplifier whose output feeds the current unit or span.
concepts.example: The ILA at site A is the preceding amplifier for the ILA at site B.

concepts.label: at the input of the multiplex section
concepts.gloss: The ingress point at which the composite WDM signal enters an optical multiplex section.
concepts.example: A disconnected patch lead between the ROADM and booster is at the multiplex-section input.

concepts.label: the fibre section feeding the unit, not against the unit itself
concepts.gloss: The upstream feeding-fibre location against which an input-loss problem is attributed, explicitly excluding the receiving unit itself.
concepts.example: Operations records the cut against span A–B rather than against the healthy preamplifier at B.

concepts.label: through the switch
concepts.gloss: The route segment inside and across an OTN switch fabric traversed by cross-connected ODUs.
concepts.example: An ODU from line card 1 to client port 8 passes through the switch.

concepts.label: the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: The endpoint or egress port that incorrectly receives an ODU because of bad cross-connect provisioning.
concepts.example: Client port C is the wrong destination for the ODU intended for client port B.

concepts.label: on the ODU path currently in use
concepts.gloss: The working or protection ODU route currently selected to carry live client traffic.
concepts.example: After protection switching, the backup route becomes the ODU path in use.

concepts.label: at either end
concepts.gloss: Either of the two client-facing endpoints that terminate the service.
concepts.example: A client-port failure at site A or site B is a failure at either end.

concepts.label: in an OTN switch along the ODU path
concepts.gloss: A location in an OTN switch that lies along the end-to-end route of an ODU.
concepts.example: A wrong cross-connect in the intermediate VB-OTNSW lies on the OTN switch path.

concepts.label: on the working ODU path
concepts.gloss: The primary ODU route normally selected to carry a protected service.
concepts.example: The direct A–B ODU route is the working path before any protection switch.

concepts.label: on the protection ODU path
concepts.gloss: The alternate ODU route reserved or configured to carry service when the working path is defective.
concepts.example: The diverse A–C–B route is the protection ODU path.

concepts.label: this port
concepts.gloss: The specific local client or equipment port currently being referenced.
concepts.example: For EQPT_PORT_FAIL on 1/4, this port is client port 1/4.

concepts.label: this switch's fabric
concepts.gloss: The internal forwarding fabric of the current OTN switch.
concepts.example: The cross-connect ASIC matrix inside VB-OTNSW is this switch's fabric.

concepts.label: available on nodes with the channel monitoring option
concepts.gloss: An availability constraint stating that per-channel power and OSNR measurements exist only on nodes equipped with the channel-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A ROADM with the option reports each wavelength's power and OSNR, while an unequipped node does not.

concepts.label: Units with the power monitoring option
concepts.gloss: An availability constraint limiting optical-power measurements to units fitted or licensed with the power-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A power-monitoring-enabled amplifier exposes total input and output power.

concepts.label: Units with the advanced monitoring option
concepts.gloss: An availability constraint limiting OSNR estimates, pre-FEC BER, DGD, polarization, and pump-health metrics to units with advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: A licensed line card reports pre-FEC BER and DGD that a basic card does not expose.

concepts.label: Each client port reports client errored seconds in 15-minute bins.
concepts.gloss: The reporting capability by which every client port supplies client errored-second counts in 15-minute intervals.
concepts.example: A VB-CP-100GE reports seven errored seconds for the latest 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: Each client port reports client unavailable seconds in 15-minute bins.
concepts.gloss: The reporting capability by which every client port supplies client unavailable-second counts in 15-minute intervals.
concepts.example: A down client port reports 900 unavailable seconds for a full 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: A degradation
concepts.gloss: A fault nature in which performance or signal margin worsens while some signal or service may remain available.
concepts.example: A 3 dB OSNR decline with traffic still passing is a degradation.

concepts.label: Hard failure
concepts.gloss: An abrupt, complete functional loss that produces an outage rather than merely reduced margin.
concepts.example: A pump stopping and making an amplifier output dark is a hard failure.

concepts.label: A degradation, not an outage
concepts.gloss: A reduced-quality state that does not completely interrupt the affected service.
concepts.example: OTU_SD with corrected errors and continuing client traffic is a degradation, not an outage.

concepts.label: gradual or step degradation rather than an outage
concepts.gloss: A progressive or discrete worsening of performance that remains distinguishable from complete service loss.
concepts.example: Connector loss increases by 2 dB after maintenance and then slowly worsens without immediate LOS.

concepts.label: slow, incipient condition
concepts.gloss: A slowly developing pre-failure condition that provides evidence of impending equipment deterioration.
concepts.example: Pump current rising over several months is a slow incipient condition.

concepts.label: degradation rather than an outage
concepts.gloss: A fault classification indicating impaired quality or margin while the signal remains present, rather than total loss.
concepts.example: Amplifier gain tilt weakening only band-edge channels is degradation rather than an outage.

concepts.label: mostly just after provisioning changes
concepts.gloss: A temporal fault pattern occurring mainly immediately after configuration or cross-connect changes.
concepts.example: An ODU_TIM appears just after an operator provisions a new ODU cross-connection.

concepts.label: critical
concepts.gloss: The highest operational severity, used for conditions requiring immediate attention because service or essential equipment is seriously affected.
concepts.example: A fabric failure interrupting all ODUs is classified critical.

concepts.label: minor
concepts.gloss: A low alarm severity for a condition needing attention but not currently causing major service impact.
concepts.example: An early pump-ageing warning with unaffected traffic is classified minor.

concepts.label: not alarmed
concepts.gloss: A severity state indicating that the condition is informational or below alarm thresholds and generates no active alarm.
concepts.example: A small pump-current increase within normal limits is recorded but not alarmed.

concepts.label: major
concepts.gloss: A high alarm severity below critical, generally indicating significant degradation or loss that requires prompt repair.
concepts.example: Loss of one unprotected client service is classified major.

concepts.label: Each channel leaving a degree is switched separately.
concepts.gloss: ROADM behavior in which each wavelength leaving a line degree is independently switched rather than all channels following one common route.
concepts.example: At one degree, 193.1 THz is routed east while 193.2 THz is dropped locally.

concepts.label: When frame alignment is lost, the unit applies the G.798 consequent actions: an ODU alarm indication signal is inserted downstream on every ODU the OTU carries, and a backward defect indication is sent to the far-end transmitter.
concepts.gloss: The G.798 consequent behavior on OTU frame loss: insert ODU-AIS downstream on every ODU carried by the OTU and send BDI toward the remote transmitter.
concepts.example: After OTU_LOF, a line card sends AIS to all mapped clients and BDI back to the source terminal.

concepts.label: The OTN switch carries an ODU alarm indication signal onwards on every ODU cross-connected through it.
concepts.gloss: OTN-switch behavior that propagates an incoming ODU-AIS indication on every affected ODU cross-connection through the fabric.
concepts.example: An AIS received on an aggregate line ODU is forwarded by the switch to each corresponding egress ODU.
